ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a velocity-time graph, with the vertical axis as v/(m/s) and the horizontal axis as t/(s). The straight line corresponding to A is steeper, passes through the -2 m/s point on the v-axis, passes through v=0 at t=1 s, and reaches v=2 m/s at t=2 s; the straight line corresponding to B is gentler, starts from the origin, and also passes through the point (2 s, 2 m/s). Reasoning: From the readings of the graph, A's velocity function can be obtained as vA=2t-2, and B's velocity function as vB=t. The two objects start from the same position at the same time, and the condition for meeting is that the displacements from 0 to t are equal, namely ∫0^t(2τ-2)dτ=∫0^t τdτ. Calculating gives t^2-2t=(1/2)t^2, rearranged as (1/2)t^2-2t=0, namely t(t/2-2)=0, so t=0 or t=4 s. t=0 is the initial coincidence at departure, not the time of meeting again, therefore the meeting time is t=4 s.
